pending_qa.q: How does passive consumption of AI-generated content affect memory encoding and brain activity compared to interactive engagement?
pending_qa.r: When people write things with ChatGPT or these AI tools, they don't actually remember, even in some cases minutes later, what they've produced because you're not part of the experience of writing it. So there's no way the information gets encoded. If you're interacting with it, then you're much more likely to remember it. A study found that the group that used ChatGPT had nearly two times less activity in the part of the brain linked to memory compared to the brain only group.

pending_qa.q: What is the optimal way to use AI tools to enhance rather than diminish cognitive development and critical thinking?
pending_qa.r: You have to have a relationship with it or it's going to turn toxic. It's going to hurt you. But if you have a good relationship with it, it can make your life better. You don't use it to do your work. You interact with it to get better work. You have to learn how to question what you're getting—is that really true? Can you explain that better?—and through that process, you help create new creative circuits in the brain that make you a better critical thinker.

pending_qa.q: What concerns exist regarding AI use in early childhood brain development, particularly for children ages 0 to 8?
pending_qa.r: Huge concerns. The best way to teach a child is one-on-one interaction with an adult who is a good teacher and knows the child. That's been well established. The problem is it's very labor-intensive and very expensive. If you had an AI trained to be a good teacher, it could improve the brain and scale up, but the question is who's pouring the morals and the values into the AI? These AIs are biased and may not have the same cultural values we have.

pending_qa.q: How might sexualized AI characters like those released by Elon Musk's Grok impact vulnerable young people's brain development and social connections?
pending_qa.r: I'm horrified. It's scary. Imagine a 12-year-old boy that's lonely gets a hold of Annie. The 12-year-old boy is going to be very distracted based on what happens in the brain at that age. The prefrontal cortex is not close to being fully developed, so the dopamine hit all of a sudden, he's spending hours with Annie and not doing the things that help to really develop his brain. When something accesses your limbic system, it begins to shut down your prefrontal cortex—you think less logically, less rationally.

pending_qa.q: What is the relationship between struggling and adversity in developing grit and cognitive resilience in the brain?
pending_qa.r: How do you develop grit? You develop grit through struggle. The way that the brain matures is through struggling. You have to learn from your mistakes. The brain was designed for that. That's what the brain is really good at—being able to adapt and to be able to adjust to new situations. When you're with the perfect partner that never is irritated with you and you never have to change your behavior to be better, that's probably not good for your brain.
